arxiv-2108-02411.title: Locking Multi-Laser Frequencies to a Precision Wavelength Meter: Application to Cold Atoms
arxiv-2108-02411.creator: Junwoo Kim, Keumhyun Kim, Dowon Lee, Yongha Shin, Sungsam Kang, Jung-Ryul Kim, Youngwoon Choi, Kyungwon An, Moonjoo Lee
arxiv-2108-02411.description: Abstract We herein report a simultaneous frequency stabilization of two 780-nm external cavity diode lasers using a precision wavelength meter (WLM). The laser lock performance is characterized by the Allan deviation measurement in which we find σ y = 10 − 12 \sigma_{y}=10^{-12} at an averaging time of 1000 s.

arxiv-2210-02705.title: Wigner molecules in phosphorene quantum dots
arxiv-2210-02705.creator: Tanmay Thakur and Bartłomiej Szafran
arxiv-2210-02705.description: Abstract We study Wigner crystallization of electron systems in phosphorene quantum dots with confinement of an electrostatic origin with both circular and elongated geometry. The large effective masses in phosphorene promote the separation of the electron charges already for quantum dots of relatively small size.

arxiv-2303-05419.title: A catalogue of precessing black-hole-binary numerical-relativity simulations
arxiv-2303-05419.creator: Eleanor Hamilton, Edward Fauchon-Jones, Mark Hannam, Charlie Hoy, Chinmay Kalaghatgi, Lionel London, Jonathan E. Thompson, Dave Yeeles, Shrobana Ghosh, Sebastian Khan, Panagiota Kolitsidou, Alex Vano-Vinuales
arxiv-2303-05419.description: Abstract We present a public catalogue of numerical-relativity binary-black-hole simulations. The catalogue contains datasets from 80 distinct configurations of precessing binary-black-hole systems, with mass ratios up to m 2 / m 1 = 8 m_{2}/m_{1}=8 , dimensionless spin magnitudes on the larger black hole up to | S → 2 | / m 2 2 = 0.8 |\vec{S}_{2}|/m_{2}^{2}=0.

arxiv-2404-14673.title: High-Dimensional Two-Photon Quantum Controlled Phase-Flip Gate
arxiv-2404-14673.creator: Mingyuan Chen, Jiang-Shan Tang, Miao Cai, Yanqing Lu, Franco Nori (野理), Keyu Xia (夏可宇)
arxiv-2404-14673.description: Abstract High-dimensional quantum systems have been used to reveal interesting fundamental physics and to improve information capacity and noise resilience in quantum information processing. However, it remains a significant challenge to realize universal two-photon quantum gates in high dimensions with high success probability.

arxiv-2405-10508.title: ART3D: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Text-Guided Artistic Scenes Generation
arxiv-2405-10508.creator: Pengzhi Li, Chengshuai Tang, Qinxuan Huang, Zhiheng Li
arxiv-2405-10508.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the existing challenges in 3D artistic scene generation by introducing ART3D, a novel framework that combines diffusion models and 3D Gaussian splatting techniques. Our method effectively bridges the gap between artistic and realistic images through an innovative image semantic transfer algorithm.

arxiv-2408-09477.title: Nonequilibrium Steady State Full Counting Statistics in the Noncrossing Approximation
arxiv-2408-09477.creator: Ido Zemach, André Erpenbeck, Emanuel Gull, Guy Cohen
arxiv-2408-09477.description: Abstract Quantum transport is often characterized not just by mean observables like the particle or energy current, but by their fluctuations and higher moments, which can act as detailed probes of the physical mechanisms at play. However, relatively few theoretical methods are able to access the full counting statistics (FCS) of transport processes through electronic junctions in strongly correlated regimes.

arxiv-2411-08234.title: Analyzing Pitch Content in Traditional Ghanaian Seperewa Songs
arxiv-2411-08234.description: Abstract This study examines the pitch content in traditional Ghanaian seperewa (Akan harp-lute) songs, utilizing a unique dataset from field recordings of the mid-twentieth century. We selected 71 songs and used Demucs to isolate vocals from instrumental tracks. We then retrieved the F0 content from these isolated tacks and applied Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) to approximate musical scales.

arxiv-2411-13692.title: Randomized Basket Trial with an Interim Analysis (RaBIt) and Applications in Mental Health
arxiv-2411-13692.creator: Sahil Swapnesh Patel, Desmond Zeya Chen, David Castle, Clement Ma clement.ma@camh.ca
arxiv-2411-13692.description: Abstract Basket trials can efficiently evaluate a single treatment across multiple diseases with a common shared target. Prior methods for randomized basket trials required baskets to have the same sample and effect sizes. To that end, we developed a general randomized basket trial with an interim analysis (RaBIt) that allows for unequal sample sizes and effect sizes per basket.

arxiv-2505-16002.title: Causal Interventions Reveal Shared Structure Across English Filler–Gap Constructions
arxiv-2505-16002.creator: Sasha Boguraev, Christopher Potts, Kyle Mahowald
arxiv-2505-16002.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful sources of evidence for linguists seeking to develop theories of syntax. In this paper, we argue that causal interpretability methods, applied to LLMs, can greatly enhance the value of such evidence by helping us characterize the abstract mechanisms that LLMs learn to use.

arxiv-2507-15409.title: PDEformer-2: A Versatile Foundation Model for Two-Dimensional Partial Differential Equations
arxiv-2507-15409.creator: Zhanhong Ye, Zining Liu, Bingyang Wu, Hongjie Jiang, Leheng Chen, Minyan Zhang, Xiang Huang, Qinghe Meng, Jingyuan Zou, Hongsheng Liu, Bin Dong
arxiv-2507-15409.description: Abstract Partial differential equations (PDEs) play a central role in describing many physical phenomena. Various scientific and engineering applications demand a versatile and differentiable PDE solver that can quickly generate solutions with adequate accuracy, and limitations of the traditional solvers and specialized neural operators motivate the development of foundation models for solving PDEs.

arxiv-2508-14342.title: Generative AI Against Poaching: Latent Composite Flow Matching for Wildlife Conservation
arxiv-2508-14342.creator: Lingkai Kong, Haichuan Wang, Charles A. Emogor, Vincent Börsch-Supan, Lily Xu, Milind Tambe
arxiv-2508-14342.description: Abstract Poaching poses significant threats to wildlife and biodiversity. A valuable step in reducing poaching is to forecast poacher behavior, which can inform patrol planning and other conservation interventions. Existing poaching prediction methods based on linear models or decision trees lack the expressivity to capture complex, nonlinear spatiotemporal patterns.

arxiv-2601-11523.title: MetaScoreLens: Evaluating User Feedback Across Digital Entertainment Systems
arxiv-2601-11523.creator: Christian Ellington, Paramahansa Pramanik, Haley K. Robinson
arxiv-2601-11523.description: Abstract The popularity of electronic games has grown steadily in recent years, attracting a broad audience across age groups. With this growth comes a large volume of related data, prompting efforts like the PlayMyData to compile and share structured datasets for academic use.

arxiv-2602-20263.title: Derived categories of quadric bundles and moduli stacks of spinor sheaves
arxiv-2602-20263.creator: Raymond Cheng, Noah Olander
arxiv-2602-20263.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Raymond Cheng, Noah Olander. We prove that the Kuznetsov component of a flat family of even-dimensional quadrics of corank at most 2 2 is equivalent to the twisted derived category of an algebraic space whenever: (i) the open subset of the base over which the quadrics has corank at most 1 1 is scheme-theoretically dense; and (ii) a certain étale double cover of the closed complement admits a section.

pmc-11406851.title: Microenvironmental regulation of tumor-associated neutrophils in malignant glioma: from mechanism to therapy
pmc-11406851.creator: Jiayi Wen, Dan Liu, Hongtao Zhu, Kai Shu
pmc-11406851.description: Glioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults, with high incidence, recurrence, and mortality rates. Tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) are essential components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) in glioma and play a crucial role in glioma cell proliferation, invasion and proneural-mesenchymal transition.

pmc-11518231.title: Does staffing impact health and work conditions of staff in long-term care homes?: a scoping review
pmc-11518231.creator: M Miller, P Hopwood, P Haghighi, E Littler, A Davis, Y Al Momani, E MacEachen
pmc-11518231.description: BackgroundLong-Term Care (LTC) homes are highly regulated and task oriented, with demanding work and insufficient resources. Chronic underfunding of the sector, coupled with increased complexity of care, has deteriorated working conditions, resulting in precarious employment, intensified and stressful work, and decreased job satisfaction. These work conditions have contributed to severe staffing shortages of healthcare workers globally.

pmc-11532271.title: Examining naloxone access and interest in secondary naloxone distribution on an American Indian Reservation in the Northern Midwest of the United States
pmc-11532271.creator: Kristin E Schneider, Sean T Allen, Allison O’Rourke, Molly C Reid, Maisie Conrad, Pam Hughes, Laura Palombi, Toni Wakemup, Andrea Medley, Melissa Walls
pmc-11532271.description: BackgroundIndigenous communities in the United States experience disproportionate rates of overdose morbidity and mortality due to a range of historical traumas and ongoing oppression. Limited health and harm reduction service access on some Tribal lands exacerbate these challenges. To date, little is known about naloxone access on tribal reservation lands.

pmc-12399893.title: Updates on Current Situation of Cutaneous Sporotrichosis: A Narrative Review
pmc-12399893.creator: Jing Shi, Wei Zhang, Xiao Liu, Mingcheng Li
pmc-12399893.description: Sporotrichosis, a cutaneous or subcutaneous infection caused by the dimorphic fungus Sporothrix species, is widely distributed in China, with a notably higher incidence during colder seasons in northeastern Jilin Province. Recent advancements in Sporothrix taxonomy have significantly improved our understanding of diagnosis, epidemiology, and treatment strategies.

pmc-12433030.title: Effects of nutritional support during neoadjuvant therapy on perioperative outcome in esophageal cancer: a real-world cohort study
pmc-12433030.creator: Yongbo Yang, Yan He, Wan Wei, Yaya Wu, Hong Chen, Yimei Gao, Wanpu Yan, Mengying Fan, Shaohua Ma, Zhen Liang, Hongchao Xiong, Liang Dai, Ke-Neng Chen
pmc-12433030.description: BackgroundWhile postoperative nutritional support for esophageal cancer is well-documented, the impact of nutritional intervention during neoadjuvant therapy remains understudied. This study investigates the role of nutritional support during neoadjuvant therapy in improving perioperative outcomes for esophageal cancer patients.MethodsA retrospective analysis of 454 esophagectomy patients following neoadjuvant therapy was conducted.

pmc-13008877.title: Comparative anthropomorphism and affective valence shape role perception and relational behaviours in human-pet dyads in Romania
pmc-13008877.creator: Florina Ileana Hica, Alina Simona Rusu, Iulia Francesca Pop, Ionel Papuc
pmc-13008877.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study examines the association between attitudes toward animals, anthropomorphic tendencies, and beliefs about the social role of companion animals (cats and dogs) in the household. We hypothesised that beliefs about the social role of companion animals are shaped both by general attitudes toward animals, including opinions about the emotional and cognitive abilities of the animals, and by a higher tendency to anthropomorphise expressed by pet owners.

pmc-13354280.title: Safety and Efficacy of Double-Effect Kissing Balloon Technique in Left Main Bifurcation Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Design and Rationale of Japanese Coronary Intervention Using Drug-Eluting and Perfusion Therapy for Left Main Disease Registry
pmc-13354280.creator: Takayuki Warisawa, Shuhei Odagiri, Masanobu Ishii, Toshiyuki Nagai, Taku Asano, Yohei Sotomi, Mamoru Nanasato, Kazuya Kawai, Hitoshi Matsuo, Shigeru Saito
pmc-13354280.description: IntroductionThe Japanese Coronary Intervention Using Drug-Eluting and Perfusion Therapy for Left Main Disease Registry (JDEPTH-LM Registry) is a prospective, multicenter observational study in 32 Japanese institutions evaluating the double-effect kissing balloon technique (W-KBT) as a novel strategy for left main trunk percutaneous coronary intervention (LM-PCI).

pmc-13413006.creator: Jacek Kubica, Aldona Kubica, Robert Gajda, Ewa Laskowska, Julia M. Umińska, Jakub Ratajczak, Piotr Niezgoda, Natalia Mrzywka, Łukasz Szarpak, Eliano P. Navarese

pmc-13662934.title: Enzyme-treated soybean meal in diets for weanling pigs: review
pmc-13662934.creator: Leidy J. Torres-Mendoza, Hans H. Stein
pmc-13662934.description: The objective of the present contribution is to provide a summary of the nutritional value of enzyme-treated soybean meal (ESBM) and review effects of ESBM on growth performance of weanling pigs. Guidelines for inclusion rates of ESBM in diets for weanling pigs will also be provided based on the published literature.
